Among the upcoming Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27, the "Passwords" app will gain a particularly powerful capability: it will be able to automatically change your passwords for you.

iOS 27's "Passwords" app can fix your compromised login credentials on your behalf, powered by Apple Intelligence

The next generation of Apple Intelligence will be the core of the upcoming iOS 27 and its accompanying software updates. One powerful new AI feature involves Apple's "Passwords" app.

The "Passwords" app was launched two years ago as a dedicated management centre for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always alerted you to any issues with the passwords in your database. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach, or if it's reused across multiple accounts, the "Passwords" app will notify you.

But until now, you've still had to manually fix those problematic login credentials yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says that in many cases, this new agentic AI feature can change your passwords on your behalf. According to its website:

With this feature, you can ensure that your login credentials are always secure and use strong passwords, while minimising the hassle and time required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will be released to all users in the coming weeks. The new "Passwords" feature is expected to debut alongside iOS 27.0, but availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you used the new "Passwords" feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
